Evidence: G20 invite, Diesel trade, Sovereign betrayal
#Aletheia #Geopolitics #Ukraine

The administration framed the G20 invitation to Vladimir Putin as a pragmatic diplomatic opening to negotiate an end to the war and secure diesel supplies.

Inviting an ICC-indicted aggressor without preconditions normalizes war crimes, sidelines Ukraine's sovereignty, and erodes Western security.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.9, -0.85) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Transaction-driven summits sacrifice international law and Ukrainian sovereignty for short-term political pretexts.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 11.5, z: 4)

- G20 Summit Invitation: FAIL (-0.88, -0.80) — Normalizes war crimes for leverage.
- Energy & Diesel Deal: FAIL (-0.92, -0.85) — Bypasses sanctions for domestic optics.
- Expert Pushback: PASS (+0.80, +0.75) — Exposes moral hazard.
Following reports of a G20 invitation for Putin in Miami alongside diesel supply announcements, former diplomats and bipartisan senators issued sharp rebukes.

The Poison:
Trading high-level diplomatic legitimacy for transactional energy relief rewards unprovoked aggression and shatters global deterrence norms.
The breakdown lies in confusing realpolitik with moral surrender. Treating an ICC-indicted dictator as an equal partner trades foundational justice for transitory fuel pretexts.

Social Physics Analysis:
Actors run a Smart Selfish Maneuver, using domestic fuel pressures as a pretext to bypass sanctions, projecting pragmatic diplomacy while abandoning allied sovereignty.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated diplomatic pragmatism and actual appeasement, it plots a direct trajectory toward Destruction by eroding global legal order.

The Unavoidable Truth: Appeasing authoritarian aggression for short-term resource relief accelerates international instability.

The Unavoidable Lie: Unconditional summits equal peaceful resolutions.

Alethekanon:
Inviting unrepentant aggressors to the table without preconditions is not diplomacy; it is an auction of international law to the highest bidder of leverage.

Awwthekanon:
It breaks the heart to watch brave defenders fighting for their homes while powerful tables welcome the very hand that strikes them down. True peace requires justice first.

Brothekanon:
Swapping sanctions and war-crime accountability for a quick diesel shipment and a photo op? That is wild realpolitik selling out actual allies for domestic polling.

Spirithekanon:
"Woe to those who call evil good and good evil" Isaiah 5:20 PASS
Trading justice and allied survival for convenience invokes moral ruin disguised as diplomacy.

Open letter to the US administration: The G20 invitation to Putin should come with conditions

Actual Article Body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin arrives for his inauguration ceremony at the Grand Kremlin Palace in Moscow, Russia, on May 7, 2024. (Sergei Bobylyov/Pool/AFP/Getty Images)

David J. Kramer

Former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for Ukraine, Russia, Belarus, and Moldova

The Trump administration recently announced that it has invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to December's G20 summit in Miami.

This invitation erodes the well-deserved isolation of Putin for his brutal and unprovoked invasion of Ukraine. Putin last appeared on U.S. soil for a bilateral meeting with President Donald Trump in Anchorage, Alaska, in August 2025. That meeting produced no progress toward ending the war that Putin started against Ukraine.

If anything, the Russian bombardment of Ukraine has only increased over the past year.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, not Putin, is the leader who should be invited to the G20 gathering. Zelensky leads a country of incredibly brave and determined people whose fight for their freedom should inspire us all.

"The only issue on which G20 leaders should engage Putin is ending his war against Ukraine."

If the invitation to Putin is not rescinded, as a bipartisan group of U.S. Senators urged, it should be made conditional on the following two points:

First, Putin should announce and observe an immediate, unconditional, and full ceasefire to the war he started, not simply one restricted to energy facilities, as proposed by President Trump, but rejected by Putin. He should not be allowed to set foot on U.S. soil again as long as his forces continue to attack Ukraine.

Second, Putin should commit to meeting face-to-face at the G20 with President Zelensky, along with President Trump and leaders from the European Union, to negotiate a permanent end to the war.

European nations have borne the brunt of assistance to Ukraine after direct aid from the United States ended last year, and they deserve a seat at the table. Any negotiation should ensure the full sovereignty and territorial integrity of Ukraine, the return of Ukrainian prisoners of war and kidnapped children, the right for Ukraine to determine its own future, and reparations for the damage Russia has caused.

Putin started the war against Ukraine in 2014, not just in 2022, and bears responsibility for the deaths and injuries of hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians, to say nothing of more than 1.5 million Russian soldiers.

Putin has been indicted by the International Criminal Court for war crimes, specifically for directing the targeted abduction of tens of thousands of Ukraine's children and their transport into Russia. He created the worst security crisis on the European continent since World War II, and it is he who refuses to end the fighting.

President Zelensky and Ukraine, by contrast, have repeatedly demonstrated flexibility and willingness to end the war, though not on the condition of Ukraine's capitulation to Russia.

At last month's United Nations gathering, 51 countries backed Ukraine in a joint statement, urging the Kremlin to agree to a full ceasefire and enter meaningful negotiations. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov countered that Russia would not pause its "special military operation" even during negotiations, once again illustrating that Russia, not Ukraine, is responsible for prolonging this war.

As the group of bipartisan Senators noted, allowing Putin to participate in a G20 Summit in the United States "raises serious concerns about legitimizing and normalizing a government that continues to attack Ukrainian civilian targets every day."

President Zelensky stated that the invitation for Putin to attend the G20 meeting could be “one of the best opportunities proposed by the U.S. side. I believe this is an opportunity for a trilateral meeting that could yield results."

When Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced the invitation to Putin, he described it as "an opportunity for him (Putin) to engage not just with the (American) president but with other world leaders." The only issue on which G20 leaders should engage Putin is ending his war against Ukraine.

If Putin agrees to that, then the Trump administration will deserve credit for helping end the war Putin started. However, in the more likely scenario that Putin doesn't agree, he should stay in Moscow, while the West ramps up assistance for Ukraine and tightens sanctions on Russia to help Ukraine achieve victory.

We welcome others to join in this call.Ian Brzezinski, Former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Europe and Policy

Michael Carpenter, Former U.S. Ambassador to the OSCE, Former NSC Senior Director for Europe

Kim Davis, Founding Partner, Charlesbank Capital Partners

Orest Deychakiwsky, Former Senior Advisor, U.S. Helsinki Commission

Evelyn N. Farkas, Former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Russia, Ukraine, Eurasia

Donald Jensen, Johns Hopkins University

George Kent, Former U.S. Ambassador to Estonia

David J. Kramer, Former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for Ukraine, Russia, Belarus, and Moldova

Nadia McConnell, President, U.S.-Ukraine Foundation

Robert McConnell, co-founder, U.S.-Ukraine Foundation

William Taylor, Former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine

Editor's note: Affiliations are for identification purposes only. The opinions expressed in the op-ed section are those of the authors and do not purport to reflect the views of the Kyiv Independent.

David J. Kramer is executive director of the George W. Bush Institute and vice president of the George W. Bush Presidential Center.

Published - October 10, 2026 01:33 am IST - Washington

U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin shake hands during a press conference. File.
                                          | Photo Credit: Reuters

Russia will immediately supply diesel to the U.S., President Donald Trump announced on Friday (October 9, 2026) after talks with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin.

The surprise announcement comes against the backdrop of a U.S. law seeking to impose steep tariffs against top purchasers of Russian oil and gas.

“I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace,” Mr. Trump said in a post on Truth Social.

He said Russia would supply another 500,000 tonnes of diesel in November, followed by 1 million tonnes immediately thereafter.

“Additionally, based on the condition of their diesel refineries, Russia will then deliver, within a short period of time, 3,000,000 tons of diesel fuel,” Mr. Trump said.

The announcement comes as the U.S. battles high fuel prices amid the war on Iran, which has become a key issue in the midterm elections on November 3.

Several opinion polls have predicted that it would be tough for the Republican Party to retain control of the U.S. Congress in the midterm elections.

Mr. Trump said the U.S.’ control of the Strait of Hormuz, along with the proposed Russian diesel supplies, would bring down fuel prices sharply.

“Between our total control TOTAL CONTROL of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST,” the U.S. President said.

Mr. Trump said lower prices for Americans, especially farmers, ranchers, and truckers, are his “greatest priority”.

“This is a very big and important announcement,” he said.

He also reiterated that Iran would not be allowed to acquire a nuclear weapon.
